items.video_title: Alternator Is Good but Battery Not Charging? 9 Causes & Tests
items.video_description:
Your alternator tests good, but the battery still isn’t charging. So what’s actually wrong?

A healthy alternator does not always mean the entire charging system is working correctly. A weak battery, corroded terminals, bad engine ground, damaged B+ cable, blown fusible link, slipping serpentine belt, parasitic drain, or smart-charging fault can all prevent the battery from charging properly.

In this video, you’ll learn how the complete 12V charging system works and how to diagnose the problem step by step using simple checks and a multimeter.

Chapters:

00:00 Intro
00:33 How the Car Charging System Loop Works
01:13 What "Good Alternator" Actually Means (Bench Test vs Load)
01:54 Cause 1: Internal Battery Failure & Sulfation
02:34 Cause 2: Deep Discharge & Short Trips
03:14 Cause 3: Voltage Drop & Corroded Terminals
03:54 Cause 4: Bad Ground Straps (Engine & Chassis)
04:36 Cause 5: Blown Fusible Link & B+ Cable Resistance
05:16 Cause 6: Slipping Belt, Weak Tensioner & Decoupler Pulley
06:01 Cause 7: Bad Diodes, AC Ripple & Worn Brushes
06:43 Cause 8: Smart Alternator & BMS Sensor Issues
07:29 Cause 9: Parasitic Battery Drain (Key-Off Draw)
08:12 Hybrid & EV 12V Charging (DC-DC Converter)
08:55 10-Minute Charging System Diagnostic Flowchart
09:48 Battery Safety & Avoid These Costly Mistakes

If your car battery keeps dying even though the alternator tested good, this guide will help you narrow down whether the problem is the battery, wiring, grounds, charging controls, or another part of the electrical system.

Always follow the service information for your specific vehicle. Charging voltage and diagnostic specifications can vary, especially on newer smart-charging and start-stop vehicles.

#Alternator #CarBattery #BatteryNotCharging #CarElectrical #CarRepair

items.video_title: Check Car Battery & Alternator Car No Start
items.video_description:
#shorts #reels #automobile 
Check Car Battery & Alternator If Battery Not Charging Or Car Dies No Start
Please like and subscribe for more instructional videos!
With the engine off, the battery should read roughly 12.20 - 12-80 volts DC. When the engine starts, the alternator should output 13.50 - 14.50 volts DC. You can look up the rated output for your vehicle, but around 14 volts DC is common. If the alternator output is under or over that range, there is likely an issue.
